subject: Storage for paperwork and equipment
hook: Files behind doors, favourites on show: planning a home office that stays tidy.
ig:
Files behind doors, favourites on show: planning a home office that stays tidy.

Most home offices go wrong in one of two ways: everything on open shelves, so it always looks cluttered, or everything behind doors, so it feels like a cupboard.

The balance that works:

Closed storage for: the printer, router and shredder, lever-arch files, cables and chargers, the paperwork you need but do not want to look at.
Open storage for: books, a plant, a few things you like.

Three practical tips:
- Measure a lever-arch file before planning shelves. They are deeper than books.
- Give the printer a cupboard with a cable grommet in the back panel.
- Deep drawers for hanging files, shallow drawers for stationery.

The last week of the year is a good time to see what has piled up.

Save this for your new-year sort-out, and see our home office furniture through the link in bio.
fb:
That quiet week between Christmas and New Year is when a lot of us finally look at the spare room or the corner of the dining room where the paperwork lives.

The home offices that stay tidy have two kinds of storage. Closed cupboards and drawers for the printer, router, files and cables. A few open shelves for books and the things you actually like seeing.

One tip: measure a lever-arch file before you plan any shelves. They are deeper than you think.
